topics.title_idea: The Lighthouse That Vanished in a Storm
topics.hook: In 1703 a storm erased a lighthouse, and the men inside, without a trace.
facts: Winstanley's tower first lit 14 Nov 1698
Great Storm destroyed it 8 Dec 1703 (27 Nov Old Style); Winstanley and five others inside, no trace found
Smeaton's 1759 replacement: dovetailed Cornish granite + marble dowels, modelled on an oak tree; lit 16 Oct 1759, served until 1882 (about 122 years)
topics.do_not_say: that Winstanley wished to be inside during the worst storm (unverified)

topics.hook: Ship owners overloaded and over-insured ships on purpose. One MP shouted 'villains' in Parliament, and a line was painted on every hull.
facts: 'Coffin ships' were overloaded, heavily insured
Plimsoll, MP for Derby, published Our Seamen 1873
22 Jul 1875 he called MPs 'villains' and shook his fist at the Speaker after Disraeli dropped the bill
Merchant Shipping Act 1876 set the safe-loading mark

topics.title_idea: The Canal That Lifts Ships With No Pumps
topics.hook: Panama's locks lift giant ships 85 feet using only gravity.
facts: Water moves by gravity through culverts and valves, no pumps
Each chamber uses 26.7 million US gal (101,000 m3) per fill
Gatun lifts 85 ft in three steps; chamber 1,050 ft long, 110 ft wide
Electric locomotives ('mules') on the walls guide ships; the ship's own engines move it forward

topics.title_idea: The Giant Ball That Saves a Skyscraper
topics.hook: Inside Taipei 101 a 660-tonne steel ball swings so the tower doesn't.
facts: 660-tonne pendulum hung from the 92nd floor, between floors 87 and 92 of a 508 m tower
Moves against the building's sway and turns the energy to heat
Biggest recorded swing 1 m, Typhoon Soudelor, Aug 2015, winds about 160 km/h
Tallest building in the world 2004-2010

topics.title_idea: The Clock That Beat Every Scientist
topics.hook: Ships were getting lost because nobody could find longitude, until a carpenter's son built a clock.
facts: 1714 Longitude Act, prize £20,000 (about £2.08M today)
Isle of Scilly 1707: upwards of 1,400 sailors died
John Harrison, carpenter's son; made his first clock at 20
Harrison's chronometer earned £10,000; Cook carried a version in 1772

topics.title_idea: The Man Who Invented Not Falling (Otis)
topics.hook: Otis didn't invent the elevator. He invented the elevator that doesn't fall.
facts: Model hoist shipped to NY Crystal Palace 5 May 1854
Per the NY Tribune (30 May 1854) he rode the platform and cut the rope; safety held
Safety: toothed guide rails + spring-loaded pads that grip if rope tension is lost
DO NOT quote 'All safe, gentlemen': no record found

rules: Nov 19 deep research on YouTube Shorts (see youtube-research-2026-11-19.json): 'How is X built' bridge/dam/skyscraper Shorts reach 300k-2.5M views; English invention-history Shorts mostly 1k-40k. The topic bank is only a backup: each run must research YouTube Shorts first, then select.
Lighthouse video: 761 views in ~4h, 14 likes, public Nov 19. Eiffel: 1,125 views, 68% average viewed. Mincemeat: 104 views, 46% avg. Pig War uploaded Nov 19 12:46Z, private.
Pattern: curiosity 'how does this work / what changed everything' + a concrete number or date in the first line beat obscure story topics. Lighthouse used a tiny 3D build look.
Title shape: 'The ___ That Changed ___' or a surprising question; first 2 seconds = the strangest fact; end with 'Which one next?' comment CTA; sources with links in description.
Every second day: run daily, exit quietly if the newest video in the log is under 40 hours old.

chemistry_ideas_2026-11-25.note: Rutvi asked (Nov 25) for chemistry topics too. Candidate ideas only: each must still be verified from 2+ sources before use. Keep Hindi 'why doesn't X / how is it possible' pattern with a number. No copyable dangerous experiments.
ideas: Why stainless steel doesn't rust but an iron nail does (thin chromium oxide skin)
Why aluminium foil/utensils don't rust like iron (self-sealing oxide layer)
Why a cut apple or banana turns brown (enzyme + oxygen) and why lemon juice slows it
Why salt melts ice on winter roads (freezing point drops)
Why onions make us cry (gas released when cut)
Why gold doesn't rust or tarnish (unreactive)
Why the Taj Mahal marble turns yellow (air pollution; check ASI/Supreme Court sources)
Why fireworks glow in different colours (different metal elements in the flame, concept only, no recipes)
Why dry ice makes thick fog but is not water (solid carbon dioxide turns to gas)
Why curd (dahi) sets overnight in a warm kitchen (bacteria turn milk sugar into acid)
Why a mobile phone battery heats up while charging (resistance, safe explanation only)
